input.subject: GiST multirange index scans can fail to return rows

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible case in message #1 (501 rows from the sequential scan, 500 from the index scan), and the fix changes one scan-time test in an existing opclass with no new user-visible surface. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 8 messages and no fix code were visible.

brief.title: Fix GiST contained-by scans that drop multirange rows
brief.problem: A GiST index scan with the contained-by operator on a multirange column can miss rows that a sequential scan returns. The leaf key is the union range, and the leaf test treats it as the real value, so a gapped query rejects matching rows without a recheck. Peter Geoghegan says this affects Postgres 14 and up.
brief.proposed_design: The patch changes the contained-by case in multirange_gist_consistent() to use a new test, so a union range key is no longer rejected wrongly. Alexander Korotkov's v4 uses the rule that if q contains r, then union(q) contains union(r). Andrey Borodin's earlier v2 reused range_gist_consistent_int_multirange() for this strategy instead.
user_visible_surface: Contained-by scans on multirange GiST indexes return rows they used to drop; there is no new syntax, GUC or catalog change.
author_claims: The sequential scan returns 501 rows and the index scan returns 500 for the query '{[1,11),[21,31),[41,51)}'.
The bug needs gaps in the query multirange; contiguous queries agree, so existing tests do not catch it.
Korotkov says contained-by is the only predicate that gives false negatives on the union range.
Borodin says using the internal predicate for every strategy would be correct but would add heap rechecks.
Borodin reviewed v4 and says the new predicate is correct.
brief.thread_state: Geoghegan reported the bug, Borodin posted v2, and Korotkov posted v3 and v4 after review comments from Reshke. Borodin's last comments on v4 ask for a comment rewording and a typo fix in the commit message, and no later version is visible.
unclear: The thread does not say whether the fix is meant for back-patching to 14 and later branches.
No one says whether existing indexes need a REINDEX; the change seems limited to the scan, but the thread does not confirm it.
The thread has no test or argument that the new predicate never gives false negatives for empty or unbounded multiranges.
The thread gives no measure of how much the v4 test filters compared with the v2 approach.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 says the bug affects 14 and up, so the fix is a back-patch candidate for all supported branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The new contained-by test in multirange_gist_consistent() runs on every such GiST scan and may send more tuples to heap recheck.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is the fix meant for back-patching to 14 and later, and does the same patch apply to each branch?
Can you confirm that the stored keys do not change, so existing multirange GiST indexes need no REINDEX?
What argument or test shows that the v4 predicate gives no false negatives for empty multiranges and for unbounded ones?
How many more heap rechecks does the v4 test cause compared with the v2 approach on the regression data?
Do internal pages use the same contained-by test, and is it correct there as well as on leaf pages?

committability.owner_note: Per the brief, Alexander Korotkov wrote v3 and v4 and Peter Geoghegan reported the bug; the owner needs to know GiST opclass consistent functions and the range and multirange code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of the new contained-by predicate on all back branches from 14, including empty and unbounded multiranges. A wrong predicate would again give silent wrong results.
committability.author_follow_up: The brief shows v2, v3 and v4 posted after review comments; Borodin's last wording and typo comments on v4 have no visible reply.

priority.reason: The bug gives silent wrong results for contained-by scans on multirange GiST indexes on 14 and later, and the fix is limited to one consistent function. Few users index multiranges with GiST, but wrong results justify attention now.

provisional_note: The fix code and messages #4 to #8 were not visible, so the correctness of the v4 predicate for empty and unbounded multiranges and on internal pages could not be checked. The claim that stored keys do not change also rests on the description only.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: unnesting multirange data types
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal adds functions for decomposing a multirange into its component ranges: unnest(anymultirange) returning setof anyrange, and a cast from each multirange type to an array of its range type. The patch was committed for v14, reverted after buildfarm failures caused by pg_dump handling of the auto-generated casts, then revised and registered in the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Only the unnest() part was eventually committed, to master and v14. The array-cast part was deferred because Tom Lane objected to how the casts were done: a proper polymorphic version would need a new anyrangearray polymorphic type. The author agreed this should be considered for v15. When the entry was later found still open after unnest() had been committed, it was closed with the remaining work left for a separate entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I still don't like the way the array casts were done, but I'd be okay with pushing the unnest addition.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pass sk_attno to GIST consistent function
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Matthias van de Meent
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch passes the scan key's index attribute number (sk_attno) to the GiST consistent function. The author wanted a custom SAOP-like operator class to look up partition bounds in the catalog and drop array elements that cannot match the current hash partition.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Matthias van de Meent objected to the motivation. A GiST consistent function is the wrong place to prune values by partition, since partition pruning is not specific to GiST or to one opclass. Catalog lookups inside a consistent function have no good place to cache results. Both suggested a planner support function, or partition pruning or SAOP array filtering in the planner, and the author did not send a revised patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: A GIST consistent function is surely the wrong place to be optimizing away unnecessary partitions: that consideration is not unique to GIST indexes (or even to indexscans), much less to particular opclasses.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix buffer pinning logic/visibility bugs in [SP-]Gist Index-Only Scans
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Geoghegan (pgeoghegan), Michail Nikolaev (nkey), Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a race in GiST and SP-GiST index-only scans, where concurrent VACUUM can remove a TID and set the visibility map bit before the scan checks it, so a dead tuple is returned. Later versions drop the idea of holding pins on index pages: they add a table AM API (table_index_vischeck_tuples) so the index AM checks the visibility map while it still holds the page pin, and they also change nbtree to use it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message (v14, December 2025) only fixes a CFBot failure, and the entry was withdrawn about six months later with no visible objection or explanation. The author had moved a backpatchable version of the fix to a separate thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rename trim_array() for consistency with the rest of array_* functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Rename trim_array() to array_trim() so it matches the array_* naming of other array functions and shows up in \df array_*. The old name would stay as an undocumented, deprecated alias, to be removed in about 10 years.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Vik Fearing pointed out that the SQL standard mandates TRIM_ARRAY(), so it cannot be deprecated. Michael Paquier suggested leaving things as they are on HEAD, since other functions are likely in the same position, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
While unfortunately named, we cannot deprecate TRIM_ARRAY() because it
is mandated by the standard.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make uselocale protection more consistent
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made the locale code guard uselocale() calls with HAVE_USELOCALE in place of HAVE_LOCALE_T, fixing a consistency issue found during analysis of bug #17946. It did not address the main issue of that bug.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut objected that using HAVE_USELOCALE as a proxy for all locale_t functions nests checks such as HAVE_WCSTOMBS_L inside it and penalizes platforms that have wcstombs_l() but not uselocale(). Thomas Munro proposed removing HAVE_LOCALE_T altogether in a separate patch, and Peter Eisentraut suggested waiting for that patch to see whether this one was still needed. The visible messages do not show the withdrawal itself; the last message has the author considering dropping HAVE_USELOCALE.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Ok, it appears your patch is imminent, so let's wait for that and see if
this patch here is still required afterwards.

precedents_retrieved.title: Check consistency of GUC defaults between .sample.conf and pg_settings.boot_val
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the TAP test 003_check_guc.pl, with an SQL version too, so it checks that each default in postgresql.conf.sample matches pg_settings.boot_val. GUCs whose defaults depend on the platform or are set by initdb are excluded through new GUC flags (DEFAULTS_COMPILE, DEFAULTS_INITDB) and a hardcoded list of parameters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier did not want the test to depend on a hardcoded list of GUCs, because the existing test needs no such maintenance. At closing he also objected to the new backend GUC flags and to the extra logic needed for initdb-set and platform-dependent defaults, and preferred to keep 003_check_guc.pl checking parameter names only. The thread had no activity for more than 8 months, and vignesh C closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: FWIW, I am not really a fan of making this test depend on a hardcoded list of GUCs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Docs: make source file path references consistent
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes documentation references to .h and .c files in the source tree consistent. It uses the full source-tree path when the text points to a file's location, and the short relative path, as in #include directives, when the text refers to including a header.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change was worth the time, since reaching and keeping full consistency costs more than it gives. Andres Freund added that every patch costs reviewers time to read, which has to be weighed against its benefit. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But the effort to get there seems
out of proportion to the value, and the effort to keep it there
over time would be even more so.

precedents_retrieved.title: PATCH: Attempt to make dbsize a bit more consistent
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the size functions in dbsize.c go through the table AM API (table_relation_size()) for tables, toast tables and materialized views, so non-heap AMs report correct sizes. Later versions return NULL for unsupported relkinds and add two new size functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to behavior changes: views would report NULL instead of zero, which also looks like a dropped relation, and sequence sizes broke. He did not want more size functions per relkind, and the two new functions had no documentation. He proposed a new table AM callback that measures physical file size and closed the entry because it needed more work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Thinking more about that, I'd be rather in favor of having a new table
AM callback to let the AM measure the size of physical files, and make
the business of dbsize.c fall under that.  It is clear that this needs
more work, so I have marked it as returned with feedback.

Index Skip Scan
Threads: Index Skip Scan; RE: Index Skip Scan; Index Skip Scan (new UniqueKeys); MDAM techniques and Index Skip Scan patch

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus search returned no earlier attempt at this fix, and the thread does not point to any earlier discussion. This is a wrong-results bug fix with agreement from three people who know the area, so no prior rejection reason applies.

This is a wrong-results bug fix with no new syntax, GUC, catalog entry or dump-visible object, so pg_dump and psql are unaffected. The only user-visible change is that contained-by scans on multirange GiST indexes now return the rows a sequential scan returns, which brings the index path in line with documented semantics. The fix is in the consistent function and does not change stored keys, so existing indexes should stay valid without a REINDEX, though this cannot be confirmed without the code. A back-patch to 14 seems appropriate.

The fix changes only the contained-by test in multirange_gist_consistent() at scan time. Stored GiST keys (the union range), WAL, catalogs and the wire protocol stay the same, so existing indexes need no REINDEX and a back-patch is not blocked by on-disk or replication concerns.

The fix changes only the result of the contained-by test in multirange_gist_consistent(). It adds no privilege, role, GUC, catalog object, log output or code path that an unprivileged user controls. Returning rows that were wrongly dropped does not bypass RLS or column privileges, because those still apply above the index scan. Nothing in this proposal has a security or privilege aspect for this angle to judge.

This is a wrong-results bug fix inside an existing opclass, with no new syntax, GUC, catalog or API surface, so it adds no lasting maintenance cost. A committer who knows multirange GiST wrote v4, and two others reviewed it; only back-patch scope and the empty or unbounded cases remain open, and those are questions for the critic.

This is a wrong-results bug fix in the existing multirange GiST opclass. No existing feature, extension or setting makes a GiST contained-by scan return the rows it drops. Disabling index scans or using a sequential scan is a workaround and does not fix the opclass. The fix changes the existing consistent function and adds no second mechanism.

This is a wrong-results bug fix, and demand is not in question: a GiST index scan with contained-by on a multirange column drops rows that a sequential scan returns (501 vs 500, message #1). Every user of multirange GiST indexes on 14 and later can get silently incomplete answers, and the fix adds no syntax, GUC or catalog surface.
